tbilisi-rustavi-ponichala-sutip.whole: ADB's completion report counts 3.2 km of new road built against a target of 6.8 km of paved road. ADB's Independent Evaluation Department says an existing local road of 3.2 km was upgraded with traffic measures and better bus stops and used instead to join sections 1 and 3, and that although this was a major change in scope "it was not officially recorded as a change". Spending came to $52.98 million against the $118.21 million estimated at approval, and $27.00 million of the $73 million loan was cancelled in September 2019, $11.80 million in April 2021 and $2.88 million at the end. On the coastal works at Anaklia, three of the four planned breakwaters were cancelled in 2018; the completion report counts 1.43 km of beach nourishment and one breakwater 0.3 km long. ADB put the economic return on the road at 6.81% at completion, against 8.7% expected at appraisal and its own 12% threshold, and rated the project less than successful; its evaluation department recalculated the return at 6.7% and rated the wider program less than successful. ADB counted 2.57 million people benefiting from the program against a 1.45 million target. All of these figures are ADB's own; no account from outside the bank was found.

peshawar-landfill-ghari-faiz-ullah.whole: ADB says the five-city project this landfill belongs to is meant to benefit up to 3.5 million people in Abbottabad, Kohat, Mardan, Mingora and Peshawar. The project's monitoring report for July to December 2025, written by the government project management unit and published by ADB as a document of the borrower, says none of the solid waste contracts had been awarded, because the business model for the waste facilities had not been settled, so no contractor had been engaged; the Peshawar solid waste package, CW-07 Lot 1, is listed as not tendered and not started. The same report puts the Peshawar water supply works at 35.74% complete against 100% planned, and the Peshawar parks works at Besai Park and Bagh-e-Naran at 84.10%, with the remaining work suspended by the contractors over delayed payments and an unapproved variation order. By 29 July 2026 ADB recorded $219.23 million of its $380 million loan under contract and $179.39 million paid out, $111.41 million of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank's $200 million under contract and $49.05 million paid out, and $3.62 million of the $5 million grant paid out; the closing date is 30 June 2028. Every figure here comes from ADB and from the government unit running the works; no independent check was found.

sahiwal-piciip-land-and-sewage.whole: By 29 July 2026 ADB recorded $188.72 million of its $200 million loan under contract and $172.76 million paid out, with the closing date moved from 30 June 2024 to 30 June 2026. The project's monitoring report for July to December 2025, published by ADB as a document of the borrower, puts physical progress in Sahiwal at 75.61% for the Lot 1 water supply works, 92.67%, 88.60% and 93.04% for the three sewerage lots, and 75.05% for the wastewater treatment plant, whose Rs 2.43 billion contract was signed on 4 June 2024 with completion set for 3 July 2026. The same report records the water and sanitation equipment, the Sahiwal road upgrading and the upgrading of three Sahiwal parks at 100% physical progress, the parks handed to the city's horticultural authority on 30 September 2021. batumi-bypass-land-valuation.whole: ADB's project page describes the works as a new two-lane bypass of 16.2 km around Batumi plus performance-based maintenance of about 200 km of international and secondary roads. ADB's own monitoring report for the first half of 2024 and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, which lent alongside ADB, both give the road's length as 14.325 km, running from Makhinjauri to the Chorokhi river, and no document opened explains the difference from the 16.2 km figure. The AIIB report says the stretch needed 5 tunnels, 6 bridges, 7 viaducts, 9 overpasses and 4 interchanges, and puts physical works at 92.04% complete on 26 September 2024, with three of the five tunnels finished and the mechanical, electrical and plumbing work at 70%. Georgia Today reported on 16 October 2024 that the bypass had officially opened, and that some residents said it was not in fact open to vehicles, which officials denied. By 12 August 2026 ADB recorded $106.52 million of its $114 million loan paid out, and the loan's closing date had moved from 31 December 2023 to 31 December 2026. All of these figures come from the two lenders, the supervision consultant they pay and Georgia's Roads Department; no traffic count or independent audit of the finished road was found.

kolkata-keiip-tranche2-vendors.whole: ADB has published no completion report for this tranche: the address for one returns an error page and the project's document list shows none, so the account of what was built rests on ADB's project data sheet, last updated 20 March 2024. That sheet lists 28 km of transmission mains, 444 km of distribution mains and 35,242 additional water meters installed; nine elevated reservoirs holding 17,100 kilolitres and two ground-level reservoirs holding 22 megalitres; and 109 km of sewer drainpipes, 7.05 km of it driven by micro-tunnelling, with one extra pumping station and 3.50 km of pumping main. It also records 22 citizen service centres across 16 boroughs of the Kolkata Municipal Corporation, a central grievance cell and 105 corporation officials trained. The project cost $286 million, of which $86 million was counterpart money, and $177.35 million of the ADB loan was paid out; the loan's closing date was 31 August 2023, ADB records the actual closing on 14 June 2024, and the sheet says spillover works continued afterwards on state funds. These are ADB's own figures, and no independent check was found.

malolos-clark-railway-row-pampanga.whole: ADB's financing covers 53.1 km of railway - 51.2 km from Malolos to Clark and Clark International Airport, and a 1.9 km extension from Solis to Blumentritt - inside a planned 163 km North-South Commuter Railway, and ADB says it should cut the Metro Manila to Clark journey from the 2-3 hours a bus takes to under an hour. Citing the Department of Transportation's December 2024 progress report, ADB puts overall civil works at 46.78%, with the six packages ranging from 4.96% for the Blumentritt package to 86.70% for N-05. The first loan of $1.3 billion had its closing date extended to 31 December 2025 and the facility's availability period to 31 December 2028. A second tranche of $1.45 billion approved on 15 April 2025 had $1,394.10 million under contract and $323.78 million, 22%, paid out by 22 July 2026. These progress and payment figures come from the government department building the line and from ADB; no independent check of them was found.

nis-railway-bypass-min-holding-tenants.whole: The EIB's project sheet describes the work as modernising and rebuilding the existing Nis-Dimitrovgrad railway, about 96 km, and building a railway bypass around Nis, at a total cost of about EUR 502 million with EIB finance of about EUR 341 million; the EU's project page puts the bypass at 22.4 km with three new stations, Nis Sever, Pantelej and Vrezina. Serbia's minister of construction says work on the Nis-Dimitrovgrad project began at the end of 2023, and the Serbian president and the EU ambassador visited the works on 28 March 2024. In December 2025 the EIB announced a further EUR 100 million loan and a EUR 34 million EU grant for upgrading the Sicevo-Dimitrovgrad section, electrifying and signalling the route and building the Nis bypass, which brought EU support for the section to EUR 342 million, EUR 234 million in loans and EUR 108 million in grants. The EIB expects average speeds to rise from 50 km/h to up to 120 km/h, annual passengers from about 170,000 to about 550,000, and freight from 3.2 million to about 6.2 million tonnes a year. No figure for track laid, electrified or opened was found in any of these pages; all of the figures come from the lender and the EU, and no independent check was found.

bogota-metro-line1-predios.whole: The line is 23.9 km with 16 stations, from the depot in Bosa to Calle 72 at Avenida Caracas, and is not yet carrying passengers. Bogota's city government said works reached 83.73% in September 2026, with 16 km of viaduct built by 19 July 2026 and 20 of the 30 trains in the country; each train is 134 metres long, has six cars and holds 1,800 people, and the city says the Bosa to Calle 72 trip will take 27 minutes against up to two hours today, with test running without passengers from September 2027. A monitoring report by the city's comptroller, the Contraloria Distrital, reported by Publimetro on 22 September 2026, found the road network and public space component 48% behind schedule and the systems and equipment and the stations and access buildings components 18% behind each, and counted 16 changes to the execution plan that had not moved the dates for testing or opening. Publimetro gives 14 March 2028 as the contractual date for commercial operation; the manager of the Empresa Metro de Bogota, Leonidas Narvaez, said the contractual dates had not changed.

mattala-airport-forest-elephants.whole: The airport has a 3,500-metre runway 60 metres wide, able to take aircraft as large as the A380, a 12,000 square metre terminal, eight aircraft stands and 12 check-in counters, and was built for one million passengers and 45,000 tonnes of cargo a year; these figures are Airport & Aviation Services (Sri Lanka)'s, given to Echelon in 2020. The same official said there had been no passenger arrivals in January 2020, and that charter flights for ship crew changes then brought about 4,000 passengers and 85 aircraft movements over four and a half months. Airport & Aviation Services and the Ministry of Ports and Civil Aviation said 2025 was the airport's busiest year since it opened, with 140,614 passengers and 703 international flights. A review by Sri Lanka's Auditor-General, reported by the Daily Mirror in January 2026, found 321,577 passengers in total over six years against a projection of one million a year, and capital spending above Rs 36.5 billion; the audit put net losses over those six years at Rs 39.3 billion, and the company's 2024 annual report showed operating income of Rs 242.2 million against operating costs of Rs 3.6 billion.
